AuditSchedule.description: An audit schedule, in one of the following formats: * `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/auditSchedules/{audit_schedule}` * `folders/{folder}/locations/{location}/auditSchedules/{audit_schedule}`

createTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the schedule was created.

complianceFramework.description: Required. Framework (set of controls) that the audit scope report is generated against. For example, `NIST_800_53`.

lastTriggerTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the audit run was last triggered.

scheduleConfig.description: Required. Configuration that defines when and how often audit runs are automatically triggered for this schedule.

nextRunTime.description: Output only. Calculated timestamp for the next scheduled run.

enumDescriptions: Default value. This value is unused.
reportFormat.description: Required. Format for the audit report.

errorMessage.description: Output only. Describes the error if the schedule is in an error state.

updateTime.description: Output only. Timestamp when the schedule was last updated.

gcsUri.description: Required. Cloud Storage bucket where Audit Manager can upload the audit report and evidence. The format is `gs://{bucket_name}`.

displayName.description: Optional. Display name for the audit schedule.

name.description: Identifier. Unique identifier for the audit schedule. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/auditSchedules/{audit_schedule} folders/{folder}/locations/{location}/auditSchedules/{audit_schedule} organizations/{organization}/locations/{location}/auditSchedules/{audit_schedule}

enumDescriptions: Default value. This value is unused.
Schedule is active and will trigger runs.
Schedule is paused and will not trigger runs.
Schedule setup failed during creation or update.
Schedule is in an error state due to persistent failure to trigger an audit. Manual intervention is required.
Schedule has been marked for deletion by the user.
state.description: Optional. State of the audit schedule. While most states are managed by the system, you can use UpdateAuditSchedule to start, pause, or delete the schedule.

id.description: Output only. Control identifier that's used to fetch the findings. The identifier is the same as the control report name.

customerResponsibilityImplementation.description: Output only. A description of how you can implement your responsibility for this control.

displayName.description: Output only. Display name of the control.

responsibilityType.description: Output only. Who is responsible for implementing this control. Set to one of the following values: `GOOGLE`, `CUSTOMER`, or `SHARED`.

controlFamily.description: Output only. Regulatory family of the control.

description.description: Output only. Description of the control.

googleResponsibilityImplementation.description: Output only. A description of how Google implements its responsibility for this control.

customerResponsibilityDescription.description: Output only. A description of your responsibility for this control.

enumDescriptions: Default value. This value is unused.
family.description: Output only. Category that the control belongs to.

googleResponsibilityDescription.description: Output only. A description of Google's responsibility for this control.

ScheduleConfig.description: Timing and frequency parameters for recurring audit runs.

timeZone.description: Optional. Time zone for the audit schedule in IANA format (for example, `America/New_York`). The time zone is used to interpret the `start_time` and the `end_time`, and to calculate subsequent run dates. If not specified, the time zone default is UTC.

endTime.description: Optional. Date that the schedule stops. If not specified, the schedule runs indefinitely.

startTime.description: Required. Date and time when the first audit run is triggered. Subsequent runs are based on this time and the chosen frequency.

enumDescriptions: Default value. This value is unused.

The audit runs monthly on the same day of the month as `start_time`.
The audit runs quarterly (every 3 months) on the same day of the month as `start_time`.
The audit runs annually on the same month and day as `start_time`.
